# Finite PM: 900-picture H.264 comparison

The bounded OFF/ON/OFF comparison completed **900 source pictures in each
arm**. The ON arm performed two actual guarded down/up/FLL cycles. Its complete
YUY2 output and the final OFF output matched the initial OFF reference; all
900 luma planes in each arm also matched a separate stock FFmpeg software
decode. Source tokens, input bytes, picture releases, EOS and ordinary cleanup
completed, followed by restoration of the matched official 1.3 environment.

This extends the [180-picture comparisons](native-finite-20261126.md) with a
single 900-picture input per arm on the current BCM70015 host. It is finite,
unpaced diagnostic evidence for [#689](https://github.com/ahnhy1324/crystalhd/issues/689).
Runtime PWM remains disabled in the normal build.

## What ran

Each arm used a fresh load of the same finite2 research module and the same DIL.
Only the module's existing finite admission parameters differed:

| Arm | Attempt limit / admission window | Input/output pictures | Physical down/up/FLL cycles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OFF before | 0 / 0 ms | 900 / 900 | 0 |
| ON | 2 / 5000 ms | 900 / 900 | 2 |
| OFF after | 0 / 0 ms | 900 / 900 | 0 |

All arms used the same `host-dwell50-twice` diagnostic client. After valid output
releases 1 and 90, it called the ordinary pause API, waited 50 ms once after a
successful pause, and called resume once. There was no third pair, direct client
register access, forced owner retirement or forced clock transition. The normal
60-second client deadline and outer 75-second bound remained in force.

The admission window starts at the first admitted physical down; it is not a
forced-wake timer. The physical ledger, rather than playback success, recorded:

| ON cycle | Down operation | Published sleep interval | Up operation | Restored FLL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 94.498 µs | 43.458182 ms | 173.001 µs | 15 |
| 2 | 106.441 µs | 42.949585 ms | 173.141 µs | 15 |

Both cycles completed without a refused or failed physical attempt, wake or
FLL restoration. The physical ledger retained all 13 records without drops;
the separate selector record was also complete. These are the existing driver's
recorded transition boundaries, not an external measurement of power draw.

## Input identity and timing scope

The input derives from the existing synthetic H.264 High-profile 1280×720p30
MP4 with B pictures. Its six-second visual content was stream-copy repeated to
30 seconds and 900 pictures. The original file, generation recipe and packet
census are retained. This is 900 source-picture positions, with repeated visual
content; it is not a newly generated 720p24 clip.

Stock FFmpeg converted only the video stream using
`-c:v copy -bsf:v h264_mp4toannexb`; it did not reencode the pictures. The resulting
Annex B input contains exactly 900 demuxed video packets and 5,335,635 submitted
bytes. The unchanged Load routine and an exact submitted-byte identity check
admitted this input before any device was opened. Every actual input call was
then compared with its admitted source bytes and ordinal token.

Raw Annex B does not preserve the MP4 container timestamps. Its ffprobe report
shows `r_frame_rate=60/1` and `avg_frame_rate=25/1`, while the original MP4 reports
30fps. The test used the maintained **unpaced** Run and artificial source tokens;
those tokens are not the original MP4 PTS. It therefore does not establish
24fps or real-time 30fps cadence, stock-player A/V synchronization, or pacing
behavior from these header rates.

## Complete output and ownership comparison

Each arm retained 900 unique input/output tokens and 900 successful picture
releases. The existing Run, Device and OutputLease kept responsibility for
output ownership, EOS, STOP/CLOSE and cancellation. The adapter copied only
validated output leases and retained owned bytes after release; part switching
did not restart the decoder, reset token numbering or split the source census.

Every arm saved **1,658,880,000 bytes** of YUY2 output in seven files. The first
six contain 145 pictures and 267,264,000 bytes each; the last contains 30 pictures
and 55,296,000 bytes. All files were opened exclusively before playback. Each
unchanged PixelCapture retained its original 256MiB cap, and each part's actual
frame count, byte count and close result was checked. The existing cap was not
raised to accommodate the larger whole capture.

The analyzer streamed these parts in global output order. The ON and final OFF
captures matched the initial OFF capture byte for byte across all 900 frames.
A separate stock FFmpeg decode produced 900 YUV420 software frames without
frame-rate conversion. Each native YUY2 luma plane matched its software luma
plane exactly. This is an absolute software **luma** comparison, not an assertion
of independently verified native/software chroma equality. No whole native
capture was loaded into memory.

## Source, checks and restoration

The run used these frozen sources:

- Finite2 research module `9cf8adc`, version `3.10.25-pmfinite2`.
- DIL built from `83f1e9c`, with its actual mapping checked in each arm.
- Private diagnostic adapter `84a769c`, derived from the retained public
  `53e6a5e` probe. It included `library-drain.cpp` unchanged; the build verified
  the relevant source paths against maintained public `cad3160`.

The private adapter adds the fixed 900-picture admission and bounded output
parts. It reuses the maintained Load, Token, CopyCapturedPixels, PixelCapture,
Run, Device and OutputLease, and preserves the LGPL source notices. It changes
no external product, firmware or installed runtime. The experiment did not
rebuild or alter the finite2 module or existing DIL.

Device-free verification passed 757 checks normally and 757 under ASan/UBSan
with leak detection, plus strict probe/control builds, maintained-source
comparison and the actual 900-packet Load preflight. Independent source review
covered token ownership, pause/resume ordering, part boundaries, preparation
collisions, failed writes, delayed close errors and closure of remaining parts.
The first build and the final build are retained separately; the final delayed
close control uses an exact one-frame capture so a count shortfall cannot mask
the close-error check.

The full official 1.3/source `24a5182b988b` baseline was restored, including
module 3.10.20 and the official userspace mapping. Its ordinary 180-picture EOS
control passed both before and after the experiment. The recorded restoration
had no outstanding process/resource handoff or restoration failure. Frozen
native records, input derivation, software recipe, both builds and the separate
analysis are retained in the [frozen private evidence collection](https://github.com/ahnhy1324/crystalhd-firmware-research/blob/4a37d361f870bc6985d4d1cc4bd3079d410e5c89/results/native-pm900-2026-11-26/README.md).
An independent archive reader imports neither the probe nor the coordinator
analyzer. Reading one frame at a time from the lossless archive, it confirms
all 2,700 luma comparisons, both complete native-output comparisons, source
bytes/tokens, leases, part boundaries, transition records and full restoration.
The original acquisition receipt keeps its pending-analysis status; separate
later results record these conclusions without rewriting it.

## Remaining scope

The 900-source-picture count requirement is satisfied by each individual arm;
earlier 180-picture runs were not added together to reach it. This result does
not by itself promote experimental PM, enable it by default, qualify unmodified
external applications, demonstrate energy savings, or establish thermal and
long-duration endurance behavior. Those remaining #689 decisions retain their
existing scope and require their own evidence.
